source: ICBM152 (MNI152 2009) average T1 brain and tissue probability maps, shipped with the nilearn package; axial slice 12 mm above the anterior commissure plane. The contrast weighting is simulated.

items.label: B0 inhomogeneity
items.cap: A change of the local field is equivalent to moving the pixel: the apparent shift is the field error divided by the gradient. Here the field error grows from zero at the centre to 0.06 mT at the edge, with a gradient of 10 mT/m, so the pixels shift sideways by up to 6 mm and the grid lines bend. The 20 mm grid plays the part of the distortion phantom.
items.facts: shift = ΔB / G: up to 5.2 mm at the edge of the brain, 2.1 mm on average over the brain

items.label: Gradient 5% too strong
items.cap: The gradient sets the position of each pixel. If it is 5% larger than the system assumes, features are placed closer together, and the image is compressed in that direction.
items.facts: the brain is 143 mm wide in the reference and 137 mm wide in this image

items.label: Metal (susceptibility)
items.cap: A metal object distorts the local field, so no usable signal comes from the region around it, a signal void, and the field around the void shifts pixels sideways, which piles the signal up on one side and stretches it on the other. Illustrative size and field.
items.facts: a metal object of 10 mm gives a signal void about 16 mm across
